message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p1 with $272 cash. I recently completed an orange monopoly by trading $300 plus Virginia Avenue for New York Avenue, and mortgaged Indiana Avenue for $110. I currently own Vermont Avenue and the Electric Company.

I now own the orange monopoly. Building one house on each orange property costs $300, but I only have $272. I will mortgage the Electric Company, Water Works, and Vermont Avenue to raise the extra cash before building.

Mortgaging all three non-orange properties yields $200. Cash becomes $472. Three houses cost $300. $172 remains after building.

Three houses on the orange properties would yield $550, $550, and $600 in rent. That is devastating. One house each would bring only $70, $70, and $80. Two houses would be $200, $200, and $220.

I can only perform one action per decision. I will mortgage a property now and build houses later. Player four is about to trade for Park Place and complete the dark blue monopoly, so I need to act quickly.

Player three now owns all four railroads for $200 each. Player four accepted a trade for Park Place and will likely build on the dark blue monopoly. Player two owns the orange properties. I will mortgage the Electric Company for $75 and Water Works for $75 to raise cash immediately.

Mortgaging only the utilities leaves $122 after building three houses. That is too little to survive a $200 railroad rent. Even with all three non-orange properties mortgaged, $172 remains after building, which still cannot cover a $200 hit. I need to find another way to raise cash.

I will mortgage the Electric Company and Water Works first to raise cash. I cannot build unevenly because the rules likely require even building. Three houses on the orange properties are the standard winning strategy, so I will proceed despite the remaining shortfall.

I cannot build evenly without mortgaging first. I will mortgage one property now. I own both utilities, so I could mortgage them for $75 each, but orange house rent is far more valuable than utility income.

Utility rent averages only $70, so keeping them is not worthwhile. Vermont Avenue still blocks player two from completing a light blue monopoly even while mortgaged. I will mortgage the Electric Company first to raise $75.

Unmortgaging Indiana would cost $121, and it is not part of a set, so that is not an option. I will keep the public message brief. I also need to verify whether the tool requires a specific mortgage value or if the engine calculates it from the space key.

I confirmed the mortgage tool only needs a space key. I decided against proposing a trade because building is faster and more reliable than negotiating. I will mortgage the Electric Company first, then Water Works, then Vermont if necessary, and build houses afterward. Two houses on each orange property would cost $600, which I cannot afford. I am now considering building just one house on New York Avenue.

The even-building rule allows a one-house difference, so I could build just one house on New York Avenue. That would leave $172 after construction, which is still too little to survive a $200 railroad hit. Three houses remain the only viable path.
